newsitem.title: UK: Cutting Tokyo business no link with S'tomo - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Cutting Tokyo business no link with S'tomo - Wolff.

text.p: A restructuring of its Tokyo business by UK-based metals broker Rudolf Wolff had no link with the Sumitomo Corp copper scandal, a spokesman said.

He also said an internal Wolff investigation of past dealings between its Tokyo office and Sumitomo continues but he could not give a date for when it might end. Wolff said earlier this week it restructured its Tokyo office and moved some dealing operations to London.
The spokesman said the restructuring "is because of lower trading volume and had nothing to do with Sumitomo's copper scandal".
Sumitomo has announced losses worth $2.6 billion and blamed them unauthorised trades by former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Wolff said in July it suspended three Tokyo employees as it made its own internal inquiry into dealings with Sumitomo. They came to London at some stage in the inquiry, the spokesman said.
